Designing calm software

Small defaults can make complex tools easier to use.

Mira Example · 8 min read

Calm software gives people clear feedback without demanding constant attention.

A useful design starts with a small number of safe defaults. It reveals detail when the reader needs it and keeps routine work quiet.

Prefer visible progress

Progress messages should explain what changed and what action is available next. They should not interrupt a task with unrelated promotion.

Keep recovery local

When a step fails, show the cause beside the step and keep the entered information. Local recovery is easier to understand than a generic error page.
